claims.text: The resort is set on the Baja Peninsula, overlooking the Sea of Cortez.

findings.quote: Set amongst the pristine natural geography of the Baja Peninsula, overlooking the Sea of Cortez

claims.text: The resort has beachfront access to one of the region's few swimmable beaches.

findings.quote: One&Only Palmilla offers unrivalled beachfront access to one of the region’s few swimmable beaches

claims.text: In the 1950s Don Abelardo Rodriguez, son of the Mexican president, turned the site into a private home and eventually the region's first resort.

findings.quote: Back in the 1950s, Baja was like the wild west. Don Abelardo Rodriguez, son of the Mexican president, spotted this plot of land from helicopter and turned it into a private home and eventually the region's first resort.

claims.text: The resort has hacienda-style architecture and an old chapel.

findings.quote: The hacienda-style architecture and old chapel make you feel like you're in a colonial pueblo

claims.text: Room furnishings include steel-studded wood doors and intricately carved wooden mirror frames.

findings.quote: The furnishings felt handcrafted: steel studded wood doors and intricately carved wooden frames around mirrors.

claims.text: The spa offers a temazcal experience, for which a shaman can be brought in.

findings.quote: The 22,000-foot spa is truly impressive, but I think the temazcal experience really stands apart...they'll even bring in a shaman.

claims.text: Guests can surf right off the resort's beach.

claims.text: The hotel can arrange an overnight yacht charter for guests.
